what_its_for: Miconazole nitrate is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin and vaginal area. It kills the fungus that causes yeast infections, athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It stops the fungus from growing and spreading so your infection can clear up.
how_to_take: This medicine comes in several forms including vaginal cream, vaginal suppositories (inserts), skin cream, powder, and spray. For vaginal yeast infections, use the applicator or insert that comes in the package to place the medicine inside the vagina, usually at bedtime. For skin infections, clean and dry the affected area completely before applying a thin layer of cream, powder, or spray to the skin. Wash your hands before and after using this medicine. Do not get this medicine in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not swallow it.
dosing: The dose depends on the form you are using and what you are treating. For vaginal yeast infections, treatment usually lasts 1, 3, or 7 days depending on the strength you choose. For skin infections like athlete's foot or jock itch, apply to the affected skin area twice a day (morning and night) for 2 to 4 weeks. Always follow the directions on the package label or as your doctor told you. Use the full course of treatment even if you feel better early.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply or use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue on your regular schedule. Do not use two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed. Try to use your medicine at the same time each day to help you remember.
storage: Store miconazole nitrate at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze the cream or suppositories. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, ears, or mouth. If you are using vaginal miconazole, avoid sexual intercourse during treatment because it may reduce how well the medicine works and could spread the infection. Do not use tampons, douches, or other vaginal products while using vaginal miconazole unless your doctor says it is okay. Be aware that vaginal miconazole creams and suppositories can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms, which may make them less effective at preventing pregnancy or sexually transmitted infections. Avoid wearing tight-fitting, non-breathable clothing or underwear during treatment, as this can make fungal infections worse.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help if your symptoms do not improve after using the medicine for the full recommended treatment time, or if they get worse. Also call your doctor if you develop a rash, hives, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing. For vaginal use, call your doctor if you have fever, chills, stomach pain, foul-smelling discharge, or if this is your first yeast infection and you are not sure that is what you have. Call your doctor if you are having yeast infections frequently, as this could be a sign of another health condition.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some relief from itching and discomfort within 1 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to finish the entire course of treatment even if your symptoms go away sooner. It can take the full 1 to 7 days for a vaginal infection, or 2 to 4 weeks for a skin infection, for the fungus to be completely cleared. If you stop early, the infection may come back.
special_populations: Pregnant women should talk to their doctor before using miconazole, especially for vaginal use during the first trimester. It is generally considered safer to use the vaginal insert form during pregnancy rather than the applicator, but always ask your doctor first. Women who are breastfeeding should check with their doctor before using this medicine. Children under the age of 12 should not use vaginal miconazole without a doctor's advice. For skin use in young children, check with your doctor or pharmacist first. Older adults can generally use this medicine safely but should watch for any skin irritation or allergic reactions.
